In RAN2#118e, UL synchronization maintenance based on SIB19 acquisition was introduced in both RRC and MAC specifications. Relevant sections can be found in TS 38.331 Section 5.2.2.6 and TS 38.321 Section 5.2a. Several issues with current implementation have been identified via company contributions in [2, 3, 5, 6, 21], which are summarized below. Companies are encouraged to refer to referenced contributions for detailed descriptions/text proposals. Clarification to use of ‘Serving Cell’ in TS 38.321 [2, 5] According to TS 38.331, the UL synchronization indication is per T430 timer, while according to TS 38.321, the UL synchronization indication obtained from the upper layer is per serving cell. [2] [2] notes that one T430 timer can be used for multiple serving cells from the same satellite with the epoch time and validity duration aligned in SIB19. However, for the MAC entity, although DC/CA has not been discussed for NTN, the uplink synchronization indication obtained from the upper layers should be for a group of cells, e.g., all serving cells of the cell group for the MAC entity. For future-proof purpose, the UL synchronization indication informed by RRC and the UL synchronization indication obtained by MAC entity should be aligned in the way that the UL synchronization indication is per cell group. and an accompanying TP is provided. A similar issue is noted in [5], which states that the wording “the corresponding Serving Cell” in the clause 5.2a is not clear and may be misinterpreted that the UL synchronisation indication is sent per serving cell. Other clarifications to UL synchronization [3, 6, 21] Additional issues are described in [3, 6, 21], which are briefly summarized below: Issue 1: Incorrect reference in MAC specification: [3] notes that for the RRC indication of UL sync/UL sync loss, the referenced RRC section is incorrect. For the UL sync indication from upper layers, it should refer to the section 5.2.2.4.21 of RRC spec. For the UL sync loss indication from upper layers, it should refer to the section 5.1.1.6 of RRC spec. (Rapporteur notes that this may also have impact to RRC specification) A proposed resolution correcting the above references is provided via CR. Issue 2: BSR and RACH if no pending data after UL sync is regained: [6] notes that if UL data becomes available during the period of UL synchronization loss, the MAC shall trigger BSR and initiate RACH procedure accordingly (due to no valid PUCCH resources), if the condition of triggering BSR is satisfied. However, UL data that became available during the period of UL synchronization loss may have been discarded (i.e. due to the corresponding discard timer expiry), when the MAC entity receives the UL synchronization indication from the RRC. As per current Spec, when the UL synchronization is recovered, UE still needs to perform RACH procedure and BSR transmission which were triggered during UL synchronization loss, even if related data triggering the BSR has already been discarded and there is no available data for transmission upon UL sync recovery. This leads to unnecessary uplink resource waste. It is proposed when UL synchronization is obtained as indicated by the upper layers, the MAC entity shall cancel the triggered BSR and stop the RACH procedure if there is no pending data available for transmission. An accompanying TP is provided in an Annex of [6]. Issue 3: Notification of UL synchronization loss to network: [21] notes that since the gNB is not able to know the exact time of the most recent acquisition of ephemeris information by the UE (and consequently know when the validity timer would expire), UE may stop UL transmission in a non-transparent way for the gNB. If/when this happens the gNB may try to schedule the UE for UL tr

[CR CR0809r3 for 38.321] Reason for change: This is a ‘clean-up’ CR, making various editorial changes, and minor clarifications (where it is thought the text is unclear or inconsistent with the rest of the spec). Summary of change: (rev 0) References are added to both sections 5.4.5 and 5.4.7 to sections on relevant MAC CEs, to follow the approach taken elsewhere. It has been agreed that Pre-emptive BSR may be used for the case of dual-connected IAB nodes, so a change is made to the first paragraph in 5.4.7, to indicate this (to align with the NOTE). Changes to the NOTE itself in 5.4.7 are also made, as the current text could be viewed as unclear/difficult to interpret. In first paragraph of 5.18.19, a ‘should’ is deleted and present tense is used instead, since the text is simply stating a fact. In the same paragraph, a ‘can’ is changed to ‘may’ as the text in fact talks about permission. This falls in line with conventional use of various verb forms. Corrected references in sections on several MAC CEs. In addition, a couple of small but necessary editorial changes are made. (rev 1) Further editorial changes to the NOTE in 5.4.7. Further corrections to 5.18.19, to remove the incorrect assertion that switching can only happen at the beginning or end of a slot, and to clarify the triggering of the Desired Guard Symbols MAC CE. (rev 2) Reverted to previous version of 5.18.19 (RAN1 did in fact agree that switching can only happen at the beginning or end of a slot, even though this does not appear in their specs). Reverted to previous version of triggering of the Desired Guard Symbols query. Several smaller typos corrected. Impact analysis Impacted functionality: MAC functions to support IAB backhauling. Inter-operability: If only the network is implemented according to the CR, no interoperability problems are foreseen. If only the UE is implemented according to the CR, no interoperability problems are foreseen. Consequences if not approved: Lack of clarity and consistency. Not following regular editorial styles. Lack of suitable references. Presence of incorrect cross-references. Some factual errors.

[CR CR0714r5 | 38.321 | Section 5.22.1.7] 5.22.1.7 CSI Reporting The Sidelink Channel State Information (SL-CSI) reporting procedure is used to provide a peer UE with sidelink channel state information as specified in clause 8.5 of TS 38.214 [7]. The MAC entity shall for each pair of the Source Layer-2 ID and the Destination Layer-2 ID: 1> if the SL-CSI reporting has been triggered by a SCI and not cancelled: 2> if the MAC entity has SL resources allocated for new transmission: 3> instruct the Multiplexing and Assembly procedure to generate a Sidelink CSI Reporting MAC CE as defined in clause 6.1.3.35; 3> cancel the triggered SL-CSI reporting. 2> else if the MAC entity has been configured by RRC to transmit using a SL-RNTI or SLCS-RNTI: 3> trigger a Scheduling Request. [CR CR0714r5 | 38.321 | Section 5.22.2] 5.22.2 SL-SCH Data reception

s 1 for a search space configured with freqMonitorLocations-r16 In RAN1 100bis, the following agreements has been achieved: Agreement: The number of PDCCH candidates per aggregation level configured by nrofCandidates or nrofCandidates-SFI within a SearchSpace IE applies to each of RB sets configured by freqMonitorLocations-r16. nrofCandidates-SFI is 1 for a search space configured with freqMonitorLocations-r16 Hence, in the field description of nrofCandidates-SFI, a restriction should be added. Wrong references to 38.213/38.212 The cross references to the L1 specs is wrong at a number of places 38.213 section 11.5.2 was wrongly referenced in a number of IEs (should have been 10.4) 38.212 Table 7.3.1-2-35 was wrongly referred at one place (should have been 7.3.1.1.2-35) 3) Correcting the need codes for some of the IEs At RAN2 110-e the following were agreed: U605: Change Need M to Need R for new NR-U IEs in PhysicalCellGroupConfig with ENUMERATED {true} the need code for nfi-TotalDAI-Included-r16 was missed in the above U608: Change to Need R for schedulingRequestID-LBT-SCell-r16 U660 (RIL I814): Change need code to “Need R” for discoveryBurstWindowLength-r16 However, in the latest spec, these changes have not been implemented correctly (still left as Need M). So, these need to be fixed. Summary of change: nrofCandidates-SFI is set to n1 for a search space configured with freqMonitorLocations-r16. Wrong references to 38.213 and 38.212 are corrected Change the following need codes to Need R for nfi-TotalDAI-Included-r16 in PhysicalCellGroupConfig to Need R, schedulingRequestID-LBT-SCell-r16 in MAC-CellGroupConfig discoveryBurstWindowLength-r16 in ServingCellConfigCommon Impact analysis Impacted functionality: The number of PDCCH candidates for format 2-0 for search space configured with freqMonitorLocations-r16 Some references from RAN2 specs to RAN1 specs Need codes for some PhysicalCellGroupConfig with ENUMERATED {true} Inter-operability: If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not: For the number of PDCCH candidates for format 2-0 there is no interoperability since the network will configure this correctly based on the new CR Wrong references exist in the spec, but this will not result in interoperability issues The network assumes the UE will release these fields in PHysicalCellGroupConfig with ENUMERATEd {true} but the UE will maintain these when the corresponding field is not signalled and this will result in a misalignment between the network and UE regarding the configuration of these fields. If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue. For the number of PDCCH candidates for format 2-0 the UE will assume any configured value other than value ‘n1’ as invalid and the configuration may be considered as invalid by the UE Wrong references exist in the spec, but this will not result in interoperability issues The network assumes the UE will maintain these fields in PHysicalCellGroupConfig with ENUMERATEd {true} but the UE will release these when the corresponding field is not signalled and this will result in a misalignment between the network and UE regarding the configuration of these fields. Consequences if not approved: nrofCandidates-SFI may not be set to 1 for a search space configured with freqMonitorLocations-r16, which is inconsistent with the RAN1 agreements. Wrong references exist in the spec Wrong need codes for some of the IEs will remain

[CR CR0711r4 | 38.321 | Section 5.22.1.7] 5.22.1.7 CSI Reporting The Sidelink Channel State Information (SL-CSI) reporting procedure is used to provide a peer UE with sidelink channel state information as specified in clause 8.5 of TS 38.214 [7]. The MAC entity shall for each pair of the Source Layer-2 ID and the Destination Layer-2 ID: 1> if the SL-CSI reporting has been triggered by a SCI and not cancelled: 2> if the MAC entity has SL resources allocated for new transmission: 3> instruct the Multiplexing and Assembly procedure to generate a Sidelink CSI Reporting MAC CE as defined in clause 6.1.3.35; 3> cancel the triggered SL-CSI reporting. 2> else if the MAC entity has been configured by RRC to transmit using a SL-RNTI or SLCS-RNTI: 3> trigger a Scheduling Request. [CR CR1871r1 | 38.331 | Section A.3.1.3] A.3.1.3 Text references using ASN.1 identifiers A text reference into the RRC PDU contents description from other parts of the specification is made using the ASN.1 field identifier of the referenced type. The ASN.1 field and type identifiers used in text references should be in the italic font style. The "do not check spelling and grammar" attribute in Word should be set. Quotation marks (i.e., "") should not be used around the ASN.1 field or type identifier. A reference to an RRC PDU should be made using the corresponding ASN.1 field identifier followed by the word "message", e.g., a reference to the RRCRelease message. A reference to a specific part of an RRC PDU, or to a specific part of any other ASN.1 type, should be made using the corresponding ASN.1 field identifier followed by the word "field", e.g., a reference to the prioritisedBitRate field in the example below. -- /example/ ASN1START LogicalChannelConfig ::= SEQUENCE { ul-SpecificParameters SEQUENCE { priority Priority, prioritisedBitRate PrioritisedBitRate, bucketSizeDuration BucketSizeDuration, logicalChannelGroup INTEGER (0..3) } OPTIONAL } -- ASN1STOP NOTE: All the ASN.1 start tags in the ASN.1 sections, used as examples in this annex to the specification, are deliberately distorted, in order not to include them when the ASN.1 description of the RRC PDU contents is extracted from the specification. A reference to a specific type of information element should be made using the corresponding ASN.1 type identifier preceded by the acronym "IE", e.g., a reference to the IE LogicalChannelConfig in the example above. References to a specific type of information element should only be used when those are generic, i.e., without regard to the particular context wherein the specific type of information element is used. If the reference is related to a particular context, e.g., an RRC PDU type (message) wherein the information element is used, the corresponding field identifier in that context should be used in the text reference. A reference to a specific value of an ASN.1 field should be made using the corresponding ASN.1 value without using quotation marks around the ASN.1 value, e.g., 'if the status field is set to value true'.
